title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1969-11-07

ai_review.summary: A high‑quality matrix recording that captures strong Dark Star, The Other One and Pigpen moments with excellent bass separation despite a few mix quirks.
ai_review.review: The Charlie Miller/ Hunter Seamons matrix restoration delivers surprisingly clear sound for a 1969 source—crisp highs, superb bass definition and enough ambience to feel the Fillmore crowd. Musically the show shines on The Other One suite, a two‑part Dark Star and Pigpen‑led numbers, though some listeners note overall sloppiness and a weak “Mama Tried” cut.

ai_rating.rationale: Average rating ≈3.8 across 14 reviews, with the majority praising the recording quality and several standout performances; a few critical comments keep the overall sentiment from being fully positive.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced matrix mix with excellent bass separation (especially on Morning Dew). Keys/organ sit a bit low in the mix and drums/bass can dominate at times, but overall clarity is outstanding for a 1969 tape.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Typical late‑'69 Fillmore flow with a continuous set, early peaks around Dark Star and later highlights in The Other One and Lovelight; some sections feel loose or sloppy but the overall arc builds to strong improvisational moments.

band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for a dominant Phil‑Lesh bass/passages during the first Dark Star, providing a memorable low‑end drive.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ/keyboard parts are slightly buried in the mix but still deliver notable intros (e.g., High Time) and add texture throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bass and drums dominate the mix at times; drum solos appear in Good Lovin' and The Other One, showcasing solid rhythmic work.
